children.translated_text: <s>Vasudhārādhāraṇī</s> (The Dhāraṇī of the Stream of Wealth)

children.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasamaye bhagavān kauśām
yāṃ viharati sma / kaṇṭakasaṃjñake mahāvanavare mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdha
children.translated_text: -<s>yā</s> (Kauśāmbī), in the great forest called <s>Kaṇṭaka</s>, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks),

children.text: paṃcamātrair bhikṣuśataiḥ saṃbahulaiś ca bodhisatvair mahāsatvaiḥ sarvabuddhadharmaguṇasamanvāgataiḥ
children.translated_text: five hundred <s>bhikṣus</s>, and with numerous <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> (great beings), endowed with all the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>.
Thus I have heard: At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Kauśām</s>-

children.text: yāṃ mahānagaryāṃ sucandro nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati sma / upaśāntendriyo upaśāntamānasaḥ bahuputro bahuduhitriko bahubhṛtyaparijanasaṃpannaḥ śrāddho mahāśrāddhaḥ sa yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantam anekaśatasahasrakṛtva
children.translated_text: -<s>yā</s>, the great city, there dwelt a householder named <s>Sucandra</s>. He was of calmed senses and calmed mind, with many sons and many daughters, well-endowed with many servants and attendants, faithful, greatly faithful. He approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and having approached, having bowed with his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> many hundreds of thousands of times,

children.text: pradakṣaṇīkṛtyaikānte nyaṣīdat* ekāntaniṣaṇṇaḥ sucandro gṛhapatir bhagavantam etad avocat*
children.translated_text: he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder <s>Sucandra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
Now at that time, in <s>Kauśām</s>-

children.text: pṛccheyam ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kaṃci

children.translated_text: -tai-

children.text: deśaṃ praṣṭuṃ / sacen me bhagavān avakāśaṃ kuryāt pṛṣṭapraśnavyākaraṇāya // evam ukte bhagavān sucandraṃ gṛhapatim etad avocat* pṛccha tvaṃ gṛhapate yad yad evākāṃkṣasy ahaṃ te yathā
children.translated_text: -n matter, if the <s>Bhagavān</s> would grant me the opportunity for answering my question.' Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the householder <s>Sucandra</s>: 'Ask, O householder, whatever you wish; I shall satisfy your

children.text: ṣṭena [GBM 1427(fol. 35v)1] cittam ārādhayiṣye / evam ukte sucandro gṛhapatir bhagavantam etad avocat* kathaṃ bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daridro bhūtvā adaridro bhavati vyādhitaś ca bhūtvā avyādhito bhavati //
children.translated_text: mind according to what is asked.' [fol. 35v] Thus addressed, the householder <s>Sucandra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'How, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does a son or daughter of good family who has become poor become free from poverty, and one who has become diseased become free from disease?'
'I would ask the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s> (worthy one), the perfectly and fully awakened one (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), about a cer-

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃ jānann eva sucandraṃ gṛhapatim etad avocat* kim iti tvaṃ gṛhapate adaridratāyā praśnaṃ pṛcchasi // evam ukte sucandro gṛhapatir bhagavantam etad avocat* daridro 'haṃ bhagavan bahupoṣyo bahuputro bahuduhitrikas tad deśayatu bhagavāṃs taṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ yena daridrā

satvā adaridrā bhaveyuḥ bahudhanadhānyakośakoṣṭāgārasaṃpannāś ca bhaveyuḥ pṛyā manāpā manojñadarśanāś ca bhaveyuḥ dānapatayo mahādānapatayaḥ akṣīṇahiraṇyasuvarṇadhanadhānyaratnakośakoṣṭāgāramaṇimuktāvajraśaṃkhaśilāpravāḍajātarūparajatasamṛddhāś ca bhaveyuḥ supratiṣṭhitagṛhaputradārakuṭuṃbāś ca bhaveyuḥ
children.translated_text: beings may become free from poverty, and may become endowed with abundant wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses; and may become dear, agreeable, and pleasant to behold; and may become generous donors, great donors, with inexhaustible gold, silver, wealth, grain, jewel-treasuries, storehouses, gems, pearls, diamonds, conches, crystal, coral, gold, and silver in abundance; and may become well-established in house, sons, wives, and family.'

Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing [the situation], said this to the householder <s>Sucandra</s>: 'Why do you, O householder, ask this question about freedom from poverty?' Thus addressed, the householder <s>Sucandra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I am poor, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, with many dependents, many sons, and many daughters. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach that <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma) by which those who are poor

children.text: evam ukte bhagavāṃ sucandraṃ gṛhapatim etad avocat* bhūtapūrvaṃ gṛhapate atīta
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the householder <s>Sucandra</s>: 'In the past, O householder, in a bygone

Homage to <s>Vajradharasāgaranirghoṣa</s> [...] <s>acaphame acapame</s> / <s>udghātani</s> / <s>udbhedani</s> / <s>ucchedani</s> / <s>sasyavati</s> / <s>dhānya</s>- [...] <s>surūpe</s> / <s>amale</s> / <s>ananaste</s> / <s>vinanaste</s> / <s>viśvakeśi</s> / <s>paṅkure</s> / <s>saṅkure</s> /

[fol. 36v] [...] heard, mastered, recited, retained, rejoiced in, and widely proclaimed to others [...] for welfare, for happiness, for safety, for abundance, for well-being it shall be. And whoever this

children.translated_text: with all provisions, and he destroys all calamities. Therefore, O householder, you should take up this <s>Vasudhārā</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s>,

children.text: dhāraya vācaya deśaya / parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśaya / tat te bhaviṣyati dīrgharātram arthāya hitāya sukhāyeti sādhu bhagavann iti / sucandro gṛhapatir bhagavato 'ntikād imā
children.translated_text: retain it, recite it, teach it, and explain it to others in detail. That will be for your long-lasting benefit, welfare, and happiness.' 'Very well, Blessed One!' The householder <s>Sucandra</s>, having heard this
<s>Vasudhārā</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s>

children.text: śrutvā hṛṣṭas tuṣṭa udagra āttamanā pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhagavataś caraṇayor nipatya bhagavantam etad avocat* udgṛhītā me vasudhārādhāraṇī prahvīkṛtā dhāritā vācitā paryavāptā idānī
children.translated_text: from the Blessed One, delighted, pleased, exalted, joyful, gladdened, filled with delight and joy of mind, falling at the feet of the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'The <s>Vasudhārā</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s> has been taken up by me, accepted, retained, recited, and mastered. Now

children.text: parebhyo vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyāmi / atha khalu sucandro gṛhapati
children.translated_text: I shall explain it to others in detail.' Then the householder <s>Sucandra</s>,
having circumambulated the Blessed One many hundred thousand times,

children.text: pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavanta
children.translated_text: having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One,
without looking back at the Blessed One, departed from the Blessed One's presence.

[GBM 1428 (fol. 37r)] <s>khakhare khakhame / dhudhume / tara tara tara / vajra vajra vajropame kaṭe kaṭe / ukke nukke varṣaṇī niṣpādani / vajradharasāgaranirghoṣaṃ tathāgatam anusmara / smara smara / sarvatathāgatasatyam anusmara / saṃghasatyam anusmara / taṭa taṭa / pūra pūra / pūraya pūraya / sarvāśā mama dāmasiṃghasya bhara bharaṇe / sumaṃgale śāntamati / mahāmati maṃgalamati / subhadramati / āgaccha samayam anusmara svāhā // ācaraṇam anusmara svāhā // ādhāraṇam anusmara svāhā // prabhāvam anusmara svāhā // dhṛtim anusmara svāhā // vijayam anusmara svāhā // sarvasatvavijayam anusmara svāhā //</s> This, O householder, is the <s>dhāraṇī</s> (spell) called <s>Vasudhārā</s> (Stream of Wealth). By the power of this <s>dhāraṇī</s>, diseases, famine, epidemics, wilderness-dangers, and the like do not prevail. Whoever, O householder, having made offerings to the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones, recites these <s>mantra</s>-words of the <s>Vasudhārā</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s> for a single night — by the stream [of blessings] with the measure of a great being, [he shall fill] his hous-

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma / gaccha tvam ānanda sucandragṛhapater niveśanaṃ gatvā cākāraṃ paśya paripūrṇaṃ dhanadhānyasamṛddhaṃ ratnasamṛddhaṃ ca / [GBM 1430(fol. 38)r1] sarvopakaraṇaiś ca mahākośakoṣṭāgārāṇi paripūrṇāni / athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ sucandrasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhagavantam etad avocat* ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yena sucandro gṛhapatir mahādhano mahābhogo mahākośakoṣṭāgārasamṛddhaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / bhagavān āha / śrāddhaḥ ānanda sucandro gṛhapatiḥ paramaśrāddhaḥ kalyāṇāśayo dhāritā cānena vasudhārādhāraṇī pravartitā udgṛhītā vācitā / paryavāptā parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśitā / tena hy ānanda tvam udgṛhṇīṣvemāṃ vasudhārādhāraṇīṃ dhāraya grāhaya / vācaya / paryavāpnuhi / parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśaya / tad bhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyair mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanuṣyāṇāṃ / nāham ānanda samanupaśyāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyā

[GBM 1431 (fol. 38v)] ascetics and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, gods, humans, and <s>asura</s>s —

children.text: imāṃ dhāraṇīm anyathā kariṣyati / atikramiṣyati vā naitat sthānaṃ vidyate / tat kasya hetoḥ abhedyā hy ete ānanda dhāraṇīmantrapadāni na caiṣā kṣīṇakuśalamūlānāṃ satvānāṃ śrutipatham apy āgamiṣyati kaḥ punar vādo pustagatā vā hṛdaya
children.translated_text: [anyone who] would render this <s>dhāraṇī</s> otherwise or transgress it. Such a possibility does not exist. For what reason? Because these <s>dhāraṇī</s> <s>mantra</s>-words are indestructible, <s>Ānanda</s>. And this [<s>dhāraṇī</s>] will not even come within the hearing of beings whose wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) are exhausted — how much less [will it] be committed to a book or to the hear-

children.text: dhāritā vā / tat kasya hetoḥ sarvatathāgatānām eṣā vākyaṃ sarvatathāgatair eṣā dhāraṇī bhāṣitā adhiṣṭhitā / dharmamudrayā mudritā anumoditā prakāśitā prabhāvitā praśastā saṃvarṇitārocitā vivṛtottānīkṛtā ākhyātā sarvasatvānāṃ daridrāṇā
children.translated_text: retained? For what reason? This is the word of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s; this <s>dhāraṇī</s> has been spoken by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, empowered, sealed with the seal of <s>Dharma</s>, approved, illuminated, rendered powerful, praised, commended, explained, elucidated, and declared — for the benefit of all beings who are destitute,
afflicted by diseases,
beset by all fears —

children.text: satvānām arthāyeti / āha / udgṛhītā me bhagavaṃn iyaṃ vasudhārādhāraṇī dhāritā vācitā / paryavāptā manasā ca suparicitā / ity athāyuṣmān ānanda utthāyāsanā
children.translated_text: for the benefit of [such] beings.' He said: 'This <s>Vasudhārā dhāraṇī</s> has been taken up by me, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, retained, recited, fully mastered, and thoroughly familiarized in the mind.' Thereupon the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, rising from his seat
at that moment,
with palms joined together, uttered this inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>):

Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, to the dwelling of the householder <s>Sucandra</s>, and having gone, observe the spectacle — [his house is] completely filled, prosperous with wealth and grain, prosperous with jewels, [GBM 1430 (fol. 38r)] and the great treasuries and storehouses are completely filled with all provisions.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having seen the dwelling of the householder <s>Sucandra</s>, was amazed, and filled with delight and joy of mind, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'What, O Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, by which the householder <s>Sucandra</s> has become one of great wealth, great resources, and prosperous with great treasuries and storehouses?' The Blessed One said: 'The householder <s>Sucandra</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, is faithful, supremely faithful, of virtuous intention; and this <s>Vasudhārā</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s> has been retained by him, set in motion, taken up, recited, mastered, and explained in detail to others. Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should take up this <s>Vasudhārā</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s>, retain it, cause others to grasp it, recite it, master it, and explain it to others in detail. That will be for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings, of gods and humans. I do not see, <s>Ānanda</s>, in this world with its gods, <s>Māra</s>s, <s>Brahmā</s>s, among the populatio-

acintyo bhagavaṃ buddhā buddhadharmāpy acintiyā /
acintiye 'bhiprasannānāṃ vipāko 'cintiyasmṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Inconceivable are the <s>Buddhas</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! Inconceivable too are the qualities of the <s>Buddhas</s>! For those who have faith in the inconceivable, the result is remembered as inconceivable.'
